title: yieldWerx’s PhotonX traces photonic module failures back to the die
gist: yieldWerx introduced yieldWerxIQ PhotonX, a manufacturing analytics platform that builds a die-level 'manufacturing genealogy' linking optical, electrical, defect and process data so photonic/co-packaged-optics module failures can be traced to their originating die or step. The piece notes the demo used illustrative data and production value depends on preserving die identity across suppliers.

insights.claim: Photonic modules can pass wafer-level tests yet fail after assembly or burn-in, with the evidence scattered across several suppliers that each use their own identifiers and test records.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Multi-supplier data fragmentation is a yield bottleneck for photonics/CPO, creating demand for cross-supplier analytics.
insights.quote: A photonic module can pass wafer-level tests and still fail after assembly or burn-in.

insights.claim: A weak optical signal at final test of a module combining a silicon photonics die, compound-semiconductor laser, CMOS die, interposer and fiber attach could stem from the laser, photonic-circuit variation or fiber misalignment; only tracing parts through assembly separates these causes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Root-cause ambiguity in heterogeneous photonic modules is why die-level traceability tools matter.
insights.quote: The final reading shows the symptom.

insights.claim: yieldWerx's PhotonX, presented for PIC Summit Europe 2026, uses the DataIQ module to build a manufacturing genealogy where each measurement stays tied to its lot, wafer, die coordinate, bonded stack or finished module, combining optical spectra, insertion loss, electrical, inspection and process data.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Positions yieldWerx in the emerging photonics yield-analytics niche alongside the CPO ramp.
insights.locator: PhotonX™ uses the platform’s intelligence module

insights.claim: The yieldWerx IQ platform includes APATIQ for multivariate outlier screening of optical/electrical readings within individual limits, SignatureIQ for spatial wafer patterns such as edge rings, and DefectIQ for overlaying inline inspection with die-level measurements, with rules runnable in monitor-only mode.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Monitor-only mode lowers adoption friction for fabs testing new screens before production use.
insights.locator: The new yieldWerx IQ™ platform consists

themes.theme: Economics of early screening in CPO

insights.claim: Advanced packaging raises the cost of a missed defect because a failing module may already have consumed several bonded dies, fiber attach, test and burn-in time; reliable earlier screening avoids that waste, but over-flagging good dies cuts yield.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Yield analytics value scales with package cost; the trade-off between escapes and overkill drives ROI.
insights.quote: Packaging changes the economics of a missed defect.

insights.claim: In co-packaged optics, where photonic and electronic dies sit beside a high-value ASIC, one bad component can scrap the whole assembly, so linking module bit error rates to earlier measurements decides whether to tighten wafer screens, change the process or adjust assembly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: CPO adoption increases demand for cross-supplier test-data correlation tools; each fix may land with a different supplier.

insights.claim: yieldWerx's PhotonX demonstration used illustrative data; its production value depends on manufacturers preserving die identity across handoffs and signals holding across lots, suppliers and assembly conditions, and on whether acting on them improves finished-module yield.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Wait for real customer yield results before treating photonic yield analytics as proven.
insights.quote: The presentation uses illustrative data to show how multivariate screening works.
